en: Bhishma said: So I have told you in full these thousand divine names of the great Keshava, who is worthy of praise.
A person who hears these names every day, or who recites them, meets no evil either in this world or in the next.
A Brahmin who does so masters the Vedanta, a Kshatriya wins victory, a Vaishya becomes rich, and a Shudra gains happiness.
One who seeks dharma gains dharma, one who seeks wealth gains wealth, one who has desires gains them, and one who wants children gains children.
A devoted person who rises early, is pure, keeps the mind fixed on Vasudeva and recites these thousand names,
gains wide fame and a leading place among his relatives. He gains lasting prosperity and the highest good.

first: न भयं क्वचिदाप्नोति वीर्यं तेजश्च विन्दति।
en: He has no fear anywhere, and he gains strength and energy. He becomes free of disease, radiant, and blessed with strength, beauty and good qualities.
The sick are freed from illness, the bound from bondage, the frightened from fear, and those in trouble from trouble.
A person who, full of devotion, praises the Supreme Person daily with these thousand names quickly crosses all difficulties.
A mortal who takes refuge in Vasudeva and holds him as the highest goal becomes pure, free of all sins, and reaches the eternal Brahman.
No evil ever comes to the devotees of Vasudeva. For them there is no fear of birth, death, old age or disease.
One who studies this hymn with faith and devotion gains joy of the self, patience, prosperity, courage, good memory and fame.

first: न क्रोधो न च मात्सर्यं न लोभो नाशुभा मतिः।
en: Anger, jealousy, greed and evil thoughts do not arise in those good-hearted devotees of the Supreme Person.
The sky with the moon, sun and stars, space, the directions, the earth and the great ocean are all held in place by the power of the great Vasudeva.
This whole world, moving and unmoving, with gods, demons and Gandharvas, Yakshas, serpents and Rakshasas, is under the control of Krishna.

first: इन्द्रियाणि मनो बुद्धिः सत्त्वं तेजो बलं धृतिः।
en: The senses, the mind, the intellect, goodness, energy, strength and courage, the body and the knower of the body: all these, it is said, have Vasudeva as their self.
Of all the scriptures, right conduct is placed first. Dharma is born from right conduct, and the lord of dharma is Achyuta.
The sages, the ancestors, the gods, the great elements and the substances of the body: this whole world, moving and unmoving, comes from Narayana.

first: योगो ज्ञानं तथा सांख्यं विद्याः शिल्पादिकर्म च।
en: Yoga, knowledge, Sankhya, the sciences, the arts and crafts, the Vedas, the scriptures and all learning: all this comes from Janardana.
Vishnu, the one great Being, appears separately as many beings. Pervading the three worlds, the undying Self of all beings enjoys them all.
Whoever wants to gain the highest good and happiness should read this hymn to Lord Vishnu, sung by Vyasa.
Those who worship the lotus-eyed God, the unborn lord of the universe, the undying master of the world, never meet defeat.

first: न ते यान्ति पराभवम् ॐ नम इति।
en: 'They never meet defeat: Om, salutation.' Arjuna said: O lotus-navelled one, with eyes wide as lotus petals, best of gods, Janardana, be the protector of your loving devotees.
The Blessed Lord said: Son of Pandu, whoever wishes to praise me with the thousand names, I am truly praised even by one verse; there is no doubt.

first: स्तुत एव न संशय ॐ नम इति।
en: 'Truly praised, there is no doubt: Om, salutation.' Vyasa said: The three worlds are filled with Vasudeva, as a place is filled with fragrance. You dwell in all beings, Vasudeva; salutation to you.

first: श्रीवासुदेव नमोऽस्तु त ॐ नम इति।
en: 'Salutation to you, Vasudeva: Om, salutation.' Parvati said: Lord, I wish to hear by what easy means the learned recite the thousand names of Vishnu every day.
Ishvara (Shiva) said: O lovely-faced one, I delight in Rama, the delight of the mind, by saying 'Rama, Rama, Rama'. The name Rama is equal to the thousand names.
'The name of Rama, O lovely-faced one: Om, salutation.' Brahma said: Salutation to the endless one with a thousand forms, with a thousand feet, eyes, heads, thighs and arms,
to the eternal Person with a thousand names, who upholds thousands of millions of ages: salutation.
'To him who upholds thousands of millions of ages, salutation: Om, salutation.'

first: यत्र योगेश्वरः कृष्णो यत्र पार्थो धनुर्धरः।
en: Sanjaya said: Wherever there is Krishna, the lord of yoga, and wherever there is Arjuna the archer, there, I believe, are fortune, victory, prosperity and firm justice.
The Blessed Lord said: Those people who worship me, thinking of no one else, always joined to me: I bring them what they lack and protect what they have.
To protect the good, to destroy the wicked, and to set dharma firmly in place, I come into being age after age.

first: आर्ता विषण्णाः शिथिलाश्च भीता घोरेषु च व्याधिषु वर्तमानाः।
en: May those who are suffering, sad, weak and afraid, or caught in terrible diseases, be freed from pain and become happy by simply singing the word 'Narayana'.

first: कायेन वाचा मनसेन्द्रियैर्वा बुद्ध्यात्मना वा प्रकृतिस्वभावात्।
en: Whatever I do with body, speech, mind or senses, with intellect or self, or by the habit of my nature, I offer it all to the Supreme Narayana.
Thus ends the divine hymn of the thousand names of Vishnu.
